proposed_caption_v6: \caption{\textbf{Without weight decay, the gauge of a linear head lowers agreement on scale-normalized geometry and leaves neighbor sets unchanged; weight decay restores agreement, and a tenfold smaller initialization, which leaves the head about as imbalanced as without weight decay, does not (Theorem~\ref{thm:gauge}).} CIFAR-5m network with the bias-free head $u=Mh$, $y=Wu$, trained without weight decay, with weight decay, or without weight decay from a tenfold smaller initialization of the head; the two runs of a pair differ in initialization, data subset, data order, and augmentation. (a)~Preregistered decisions at $N=250{,}000$: the number of the 96 disjoint pairs within the frozen tolerance $\varepsilon$, shaded by decision. Rows follow the lattice, with order criteria below the dashed line. Outlined cells are preregistered, and crosses mark our two failed predictions, that $u$ without weight decay would disagree on neighbor sets and that small initialization would act like weight decay on $G_s$. (b)~Exploratory: fraction of pairs whose $G_s$ discrepancy lies below a threshold, in units of $\varepsilon$, for $u$ (solid) and $y$ (dashed); grey lines are the decision levels, and the dotted line is the secondary tolerance. (c)~Exploratory: paired excess $\Delta(u)-\Delta(y)$ of each pair of runs, positive when the heads of the pair disagree more than their outputs. Dots are pairs, bars medians, and open circles the eight pilot pairs per arm at $N=100{,}000$ that set $\varepsilon$. The number after each arm in the key is the median relative imbalance of its head at the end of training at $N=250{,}000$. Table~\ref{tab:app-s22-full} gives every decision, Table~\ref{tab:app-s22-excess} the excess on every criterion, and Table~\ref{tab:app-s22-decomp} its split into a gauge common to both runs of a pair and their mismatch.}
caption_v8: \caption{\textbf{Without weight decay, the gauge of a linear head lowers agreement on scale-normalized geometry and leaves neighbor sets unchanged, and weight decay restores agreement (Theorem~\ref{thm:gauge}).} (a)~Fraction of disjoint pairs of CIFAR-5m runs at $N=250{,}000$ whose head coordinates $u$ lie within the frozen tolerance $\varepsilon$, with the preregistered predictions boxed in black. (b)~The same fraction on $G_s$ against the threshold, for $u$ (solid) and the outputs $y$ (dashed). Grey lines are the decision levels. (c)~Excess $\Delta(u)-\Delta(y)$ per pair of runs, with median bars and the arms ordered as in (a). Panels (b) and (c) are exploratory, and Table~\ref{tab:app-s22-full} gives every decision.}

kept_messages.a: the preregistered decision of every u cell at 250,000 (now a mark against the decision lines): weight decay reliable everywhere; no weight decay unreliable on G_s, inconclusive on 1 - CKA, reliable on Delta_Pi, T_G/Aff, SOG, order criteria and T_N,10; small init. inconclusive on G_s and 1 - CKA; v8 r2: the preregistered predictions as boxes, with the two failed predictions visible as marks outside their boxes
kept_messages.b: the knife edge of G_s without weight decay (its u curve crosses the decision band at eps)
kept_messages.c: the gauge raises the G_s and 1 - CKA discrepancy of u over y without weight decay and under small init., leaves T_N,10 at zero, and lowers T_E; weight decay removes it
